title: Measuring Agents in Production
abstract: This ICML 2026 study reports evidence from 20 in-depth case studies and 86 deployed agent systems across 26 domains. The authors report that 68% of deployed agents execute at most ten steps before human intervention, 70% rely on prompting off-the-shelf models rather than weight tuning, and 74% primarily depend on human evaluation. Reliability remains the leading development challenge, and teams commonly address it through bounded workflows and systems-level controls.

title: ComplexMCP: Evaluation of LLM Agents in Dynamic, Interdependent, and Large-Scale Tool Sandbox
abstract: ComplexMCP evaluates language-model agents with more than 300 tools across seven stateful sandboxes that include interdependent tools and simulated API failures. The ICML 2026 paper reports that evaluated top-tier models remained below 60% task success while human performance reached 90%. Its trajectory analysis identifies tool-retrieval saturation, skipped environment verification, and failure-recovery behavior as important production bottlenecks.

title: ITBench: Evaluating AI Agents across Diverse Real-World IT Automation Tasks
abstract: ITBench is an ICML 2025 benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real-world IT automation tasks. Its initial release covers Site Reliability Engineering, compliance and security operations, and financial operations. The work emphasizes reproducible environments and effectiveness measurement for agents expected to operate critical cloud and enterprise workflows.

raw.seed_reason: AI for cloud operations and industry automation

title: ServeGen: Workload Characterization and Generation of Large Language Model Serving in Production
abstract: ServeGen presents an analysis of production LLM-serving workloads from a worldwide cloud service. The NSDI 2026 work covers language, multimodal, and reasoning-model traffic and develops a workload generator intended to reproduce important production characteristics. It provides evidence for designing and evaluating cloud infrastructure around the behavior of actual AI applications rather than simplified synthetic assumptions.

title: DEEPSERVE: Serverless Large Language Model Serving at Scale
abstract: DEEPSERVE describes a serverless platform for serving and fine-tuning large language models in cloud environments. The USENIX ATC 2025 paper reports that the platform operated in production for more than a year on a large accelerator cluster and provided model, fine-tuning, and agent-serving APIs. The system is relevant to startup and enterprise decisions about elasticity, utilization, latency, and the operational complexity of AI infrastructure.

title: AIOpsLab: A Holistic Framework to Evaluate AI Agents for Enabling Autonomous Clouds
abstract: AIOpsLab proposes a framework for evaluating AI agents across the cloud-incident lifecycle, including detection, localization, root-cause analysis, and mitigation. The authors describe the longer-term idea of AgentOps: agents participating in self-healing cloud systems. The work is a preprint and should be treated as an emerging research direction rather than established production evidence.
